qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Modest switching costs in core commercial treasury management and retail deposit relationships in the Midwest and Southeast. However, fails empirical proof of moat: 10-year median ROIC is 9.5% (< 12% hurdle), with through-the-cycle ROE ~10-12% and ROA ~1.1-1.2%. The bank is a price-taker on both lending spreads and deposit betas, lacking structural pricing power >= inflation against money-center peers, money market funds, and fintechs.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Multi-cycle ROIC median is 9.5%, consistently below the 12% Munger hurdle across the credit cycle. Fifth Third operates as a regional commercial price-taker on both lending spreads and deposit betas, lacking independent pricing power >= inflation against national money-center banks (JPMorgan, BofA) and digital alternatives. The $10.9B Comerica acquisition expands footprint into Texas/California but adds substantial integration risk without curing structural spread-business economics.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of 9.5% fails the 12% capital efficiency hurdle. Full-year ROE of 11.9% in 2024 and ~12.2-12.6% in 2025 reflects typical regional bank profitability, highly levered (~10-12x assets to tangible equity) with ROA hovering around 1.1-1.3%. Net interest income ($6.0B in 2025) is cyclical and vulnerable to deposit repricing and yield curve dynamics. In July 2024, the CFPB ordered $20M in penalties and restitution over unauthorized fake customer accounts and forced auto-loan insurance repossessions, highlighting historical sales-practice vulnerabilities. In 2025-2026, FITB completed an all-stock $10.9B acquisition of Comerica, expanding assets past $300B and branch count to ~1,500 across the Midwest, Southeast, Texas, and California, but increasing operational integration complexity while commercial banking remains structurally commoditized.
